notes:
### 1. Apportionment Formula
* **Fact:** North Carolina uses a **single sales factor** (100% receipts/sales factor) to apportion multistate business income. Apportionable income of a corporation is apportioned by multiplying income by the sales factor determined under subsection (l).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (no changes between them).
* **Official URL:** https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-130.4.html (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-130.4(i))

---

### 2. Sourcing of Receipts from Services and Intangibles
* **Fact:** 
  * **Market-based sourcing** applies to both services and intangibles.
  * *Services:* Receipts from services are sourced to North Carolina if the taxpayer’s market for the receipts is in North Carolina.
  * *Intangibles:* Receipts from the rental, lease, licensing, or sale of intangible property are sourced to North Carolina if and to the extent the intangible property is used in the state.
  * *Exception/Alternative:* Under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-130.4(t3), taxpayers with an existing State net loss balance as of the end of the 2019 tax year that made a binding election on their 2020 return may continue to apportion receipts from services based on the percentage of **income-producing activities** performed in North Carolina (cost of performance) until that pre-2020 loss balance is fully utilized or expired.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (no changes between them).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-130.4.html (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-130.4(l), (t3))
  * https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/market-based-sourcing

---

### 3. Industries with Special Apportionment Formulas
North Carolina prescribes specific statutory apportionment formulas or industry-specific sourcing rules for the following industries:

* **Railroad Companies:** Apportioned using a single railway operating revenue factor: railway operating revenue from business done within North Carolina divided by total railway operating revenue everywhere (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-130.4(m)).
* **Motor Carriers (Property or Passengers):** Apportioned using a vehicle mileage fraction: vehicle miles in North Carolina divided by total vehicle miles everywhere (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-130.4(o)).
* **Air and Water Transportation Corporations:** Apportioned using a revenue ton mile fraction: revenue ton miles in North Carolina divided by revenue ton miles everywhere (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-130.4(s)). A qualified air freight forwarder uses the factor of its affiliated air carrier.
* **Pipeline Companies (Petroleum-based liquids or natural gas subject to FERC regulation):** Apportioned using a traffic unit fraction: traffic units in North Carolina divided by total traffic units everywhere (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-130.4(s2)).
* **Wholesale Content Distributors:** Apportioned using industry-specific market-based customer/billing sourcing rules; income apportioned to North Carolina cannot be less than 2% of total domestic gross receipts from advertising and licensing activities (N.C. Gen. Stat. §§ 105-130.4(l1), 105-130.4A).
* **Banks:** Apportioned using industry-specific market-based sourcing rules for interest, service fees, and financial receipts (N.C. Gen. Stat. §§ 105-130.4(l2), 105-130.4B).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (no changes between them).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-130.4.html
  * https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-130.4A.html
  * https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-130.4B.html

---

### 4. Form / Schedule Used to Compute Apportionment
* **Fact:** 
  * **Schedule O** (*Computation of Apportionment Factor*) of **Form CD-405** (C-Corporation Tax Return) or **Form CD-401S** (S-Corporation Tax Return).
  * *(For partnerships: Form D-403, Part 2)*.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (no changes between them).
* **Official URL:** https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/corporate-tax-forms-and-instructions

### 1. Corporate Income and Franchise Tax Nexus

* **Nexus Standard ("Doing Business"):** 
  * North Carolina imposes corporate income tax on corporations "doing business in this State" (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-130.3) and franchise tax on corporations incorporated in NC, holding a certificate of authority, or "doing business in this State" (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-122).
  * "Doing business" is defined by statute as "[e]ach and every act, power, or privilege exercised or enjoyed in this State, as an incident to, or by virtue of the powers and privileges granted by the laws of this State" (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-114(b)(3)).
  * Administrative rule 17 NCAC 05C .0102 provides that "doing business" includes the operation of any enterprise or activity in North Carolina for economic gain, including:
    * Maintaining an office or place of business.
    * Maintaining an inventory of goods/merchandise.
    * Selling or distributing merchandise via employees or agents.
    * Rendering services to clients or customers in NC through employees or agents.
    * Owending, renting, or operating business or income-producing property (realty, tangible personal property, trademarks, trade names, franchise rights, computer programs, copyrights, patented processes, and licenses).
* **Bright-Line / Factor-Presence Economic Nexus Threshold:**
  * **General corporate income/franchise tax:** **Not found.** North Carolina has not enacted a general bright-line factor-presence dollar threshold (e.g., standard MTC factor-presence dollar thresholds for sales, property, or payroll) for corporate income or franchise tax.
  * **Mortgage lenders (specific rule):** Under Directive CD-99-1, an out-of-state mortgage lender without a physical place of business is doing business if it makes more than **$5,000,000** of loans secured by NC real property *and* uses employees, agents, or contractors to perform services/activities in the state.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * NCDOR FAQ on Nexus ("Physical Presence" vs. "Economic Presence"): https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/frequently-asked-questions-and-important-notices/frequently-asked-questions-about-nc-franchise-corporate-income-and-insurance-tax
  * NCDOR 2025 Corporate Income, Franchise, and Insurance Tax Bulletin: https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/corporate-income-franchise-and-insurance-tax-bulletins
  * NCDOR Directive CD-99-1: https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/corporate-taxes-directives-technical-advice-memoranda/directive-cd-99-1
  * N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-114: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-114.html

---

### 2. Remote Seller Economic Nexus Threshold (Sales and Use Tax)

* **Sales Threshold:** Gross sales in excess of **$100,000** sourced to North Carolina, including remote sales and sales made as or facilitated through a marketplace seller/facilitator (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-164.8(b)(9)).
* **Transaction Count:** **None.** Effective July 1, 2024, Session Law 2024-28 repealed the 200-transaction threshold. For tax years 2025 and 2026, there is no transaction threshold.
* **Measurement Period:** The previous or current calendar year.
* **Registration & Collection Timing:**
  * *Tax Year 2025 through July 1, 2026:* Sellers must register and collect sales tax effective 60 days after meeting the threshold.
  * *Effective July 2, 2026:* A remote retailer meeting the threshold as the sole basis of nexus becomes engaged in business on the first day of the first calendar month occurring at least 60 days after exceeding the threshold.
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026 (with the administrative compliance timing adjustment effective July 2, 2026).
* **Official Sources:**
  * NCDOR Remote Sales Guidance: https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/sales-and-use-tax/remote-sales
  * NCDOR Directive SD-24-1 (Repeal of Transaction Threshold): https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/sales-and-use-tax/sales-and-use-tax-directives/sales-and-use-tax-directive-sd-24-1
  * NCDOR Notice on Extended Compliance Period: https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/sales-and-use-tax/important-notices-issued-sales-and-use-tax-division/important-notice-extended-compliance-period-certain-remote-sellers
  * N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-164.8: https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-164.8.html

---

### 3. North Carolina's Stated Position on P.L. 86-272 Protection

* **Corporate Income Tax:** North Carolina recognizes Public Law 86-272 (15 U.S.C. § 381) as limiting its jurisdiction to impose corporate net income tax when a corporation's only activity within the state is the solicitation of orders for sales of tangible personal property, provided orders are sent outside North Carolina for approval and filled from an out-of-state location.
* **Corporate Franchise Tax:** The Department explicitly maintains that **P.L. 86-272 does not apply to the North Carolina franchise tax**. Because the franchise tax is a privilege/excise tax rather than an income tax, a corporation protected from corporate income tax under P.L. 86-272 remains subject to the franchise tax and must file Form CD-405/CD-401S to pay franchise tax if it is doing business in North Carolina.
* **MTC Revised Interpretation (Internet Activities):** **Not found.** The North Carolina Department of Revenue has not published administrative guidance, directives, or rules addressing or adopting the Multistate Tax Commission’s (MTC) revised interpretation regarding internet/website activities under P.L. 86-272.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 without change.
* **Official Sources:**
  * NCDOR Directive CD-98-4 (Doing Business / P.L. 86-272 and Franchise Tax): https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/corporate-taxes-directives-technical-advice-memoranda/directive-cd-98-4
  * NCDOR Form CD-405 Instructions (C-Corporation Tax Return): https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/corporate-tax-forms-and-instructions/cd-405-c-corporation-tax-return-instructions
  * NCDOR 2025 Corporate Income, Franchise, and Insurance Tax Bulletin: https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/corporate-income-franchise-and-insurance-tax-bulletins

notes:
### 1. Individual Income Tax Rate
* **Tax Year 2025:** Flat rate of **4.25%** (0.0425) on North Carolina taxable income.
* **Tax Year 2026:** Flat rate of **3.99%** (0.0399) on North Carolina taxable income.
* **Official URL:** https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/individual-income-tax/tax-rate-schedules

---

### 2. Corporate Income Tax Rate and Minimum Tax
* **Tax Year 2025:** Flat rate of **2.25%** on net taxable income.
* **Tax Year 2026:** Flat rate of **2.00%** on net taxable income.
* **Minimum Tax:** **None** (North Carolina does not impose a minimum corporate income tax; minimum tax applies under the franchise tax).
* **Official URL:** https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/corporate-income-and-franchise-tax-rates

---

### 3. State Sales and Use Tax Rate & Local Rates
* **State Rate (2025 & 2026):** **4.75%** general State sales and use tax rate.
* **Local Jurisdictions:** Yes, local jurisdictions add rates. Counties levy local sales and use taxes of **2.00%** or **2.25%**, plus an optional transit rate of **0.50%**, making combined rates typically 6.75% to 7.50%. Effective July 1, 2026, Mecklenburg County levied an additional **1.00%** local sales and use tax, bringing its total rate to **8.25%**.
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/sales-and-use-tax/sales-and-use-tax-rates
  * https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/sales-and-use-tax/sales-and-use-tax-rates/current-sales-and-use-tax-rates

---

### 4. Gross Receipts, Franchise, Margin, or Other Notable Business Taxes
* **Franchise Tax (Applies to both 2025 and 2026):**
  * Imposed on corporations chartered in or doing business in North Carolina based on their apportioned net worth base.
  * **C-Corporations:** **$1.50 per $1,000** of the tax base, with a maximum of **$500** for the first **$1,000,000** of the tax base.
  * **S-Corporations:** **$200** for the first **$1,000,000** of the tax base, and **$1.50 per $1,000** of the tax base exceeding **$1,000,000**.
  * **Holding Companies:** Maximum of **$500** for the first **$1,000,000** of base and **$1.50 per $1,000** on the excess, subject to a total maximum tax of **$150,000**.
  * **Minimum Franchise Tax:** **$200** annually for both active and inactive corporations.
* **Gross Receipts / Privilege Taxes (2025 & 2026):**
  * North Carolina does not levy a general gross receipts or margin tax.
  * State Privilege License taxes (under G.S. Chapter 105, Article 2) apply to specific select businesses (such as loan agencies, check cashers, and pawnbrokers; general professional privilege licenses were repealed effective July 1, 2024).
  * A **7.00%** combined general rate applies to gross receipts/sales price from utilities and select services (telecommunications, electricity, piped natural gas, video programming).
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/corporate-income-and-franchise-tax-rates
  * https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/privilege-license-tax

notes:
### 1. Individual Return Due Dates & Extension Rules
* **Calendar-Year Due Date:** April 15 (or the next business day if April 15 falls on a weekend or legal holiday).
* **Extension Duration:** 6 months (to October 15).
* **How Extensions Work:**
  * **Automatic State Extension:** A taxpayer granted an automatic federal extension (Form 4868) is granted an automatic North Carolina extension by checking the "Federal Extension" circle on Form D-400.
  * **Form D-410:** Taxpayers not granted a federal extension must file Form D-410 (*Application for Extension for Filing Individual Income Tax Return*) by the original statutory due date.
  * **Payment Requirement:** An extension of time to file is not an extension to pay. The late-payment penalty will not apply if the taxpayer pays at least 90% of the tax liability through withholding, estimated payments, or with Form D-410 by the original due date, and pays the balance with the return; statutory interest accrues daily on any unpaid tax from the original due date.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both Tax Year 2025 and Tax Year 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * [NCDOR: Individual Income Tax Extensions](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes/individual-income-tax/extensions)
  * [NCDOR: FAQs About Filing an Application for Extension to File Your NC Individual Income Tax Return](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/individual-income-tax/extensions/frequently-asked-questions-about-filing-application-extension-file-your-nc-individual-income-tax-return)

---

### 2. Corporate & Pass-Through Return Due Dates & Extensions
* **C-Corporations (Form CD-405) & S-Corporations (Form CD-401S):**
  * **Statutory Due Date:** 15th day of the 4th month following the close of the income year (April 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **Extension Rule & Duration Change:** 
    * *Prior to 2025:* 6-month extension.
    * *Tax Years 2025 & 2026:* Effective for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, the extension period is **7 months** from the original due date (November 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **How to Obtain:** Automatic state extension if granted a federal extension (by checking the "Federal Extension" circle on the return), or by filing Form CD-419 (*Application for Extension for Franchise and Corporate Tax*) by the statutory due date. Does not extend the time to pay tax.
* **Partnerships (Form D-403):**
  * **Statutory Due Date:** 15th day of the 4th month following the close of the tax year (April 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **Extension Duration:** 6-month extension (to October 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **How to Obtain:** Automatic state extension if granted an automatic federal extension (by checking the "Federal Extension" circle on Form D-403); otherwise, file Form D-410P (*Application for Extension for Filing Partnership, Estate, or Trust Tax Return*) by the original due date. Does not extend the time to pay.
* **Applicability:** Applies to Tax Years 2025 and 2026 (note corporate extension length changed from 6 to 7 months beginning TY 2025).
* **Official Sources:**
  * [NCDOR: Corporate Income & Franchise Tax Extensions](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes/corporate-income-franchise-tax/extensions)
  * [NCDOR: Notice - Extension of Time To File Franchise and Corporate Income Tax Return](https://www.ncdor.gov/news/important-notices/important-notice-extension-time-file-franchise-and-corporate-income-tax-return)
  * [NCDOR: Corporate Filing Requirements](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes/corporate-income-franchise-tax/filing-requirements)

---

### 3. Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET)
* **Existence:** Yes. North Carolina enacted an entity-level elective tax under N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-154.1 (Taxed Partnerships) and § 105-131.1A (Taxed S Corporations).
* **Tax Rate:** Imposed at the individual income tax rate pursuant to G.S. § 105-153.7:
  * **Tax Year 2025:** **4.25%**
  * **Tax Year 2026:** **3.99%** (rate reduced for taxable years beginning after 2025 per S.L. 2023-134 / G.S. § 105-153.7(a)).
* **How and When to Elect:**
  * Made annually on the timely filed North Carolina annual return (Form D-403 for partnerships; Form CD-401S for S Corporations) by answering "Yes" to the Taxed PTE question on page 1.
  * Must be elected on or before the due date of the return, including extensions.
  * Under G.S. § 105-154.1(a) and G.S. § 105-131.1A, the election **cannot be made or revoked after the return is filed**.
* **Official Sources:**
  * [N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-154.1](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-154.1.html)
  * [N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-153.7](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-153.7.html)
  * [NCDOR: Notice Regarding Pass-Through Entity Tax](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/important-notices-and-faqs/important-notice-regarding-north-carolinas-recently-enacted-pass-through-entity-tax)
  * [NCDOR: 2025 Personal Taxes Law Changes](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/individual-income-tax/2025-personal-taxes-law-changes)

---

### 4. Composite / Group Nonresident Returns
* **S-Corporations:** Permitted under G.S. § 105-131.7(b) to file a composite return and make composite payments of tax on behalf of qualifying nonresident shareholders directly on Form CD-401S. 
  * Nonresident shareholders who choose not to be included in a composite return or PTET election must provide a signed Form NC-NA (*Nonresident Shareholder Agreement*) agreeing to NC tax jurisdiction and individual filing; absent this, the corporation must pay the tax on their behalf.
* **Partnerships:** North Carolina does not use a separate composite return form for partnerships; instead, under G.S. § 105-154(d), partnerships report and pay tax directly on Form D-403 (Part 4) on behalf of nonresident partners (unless an exemption applies).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both Tax Year 2025 and Tax Year 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * [N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-131.7](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_105/GS_105-131.7.html)
  * [NCDOR: 2025 CD-401S S-Corporation Tax Return Instructions](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/corporate-income-franchise-tax/corporate-tax-forms-and-instructions/cd-401s-instructions-s-corporation-tax-return-2025)

---

### 5. Estimated Tax & Nonresident Withholding for Pass-Throughs
* **Nonresident Withholding / Entity Payment Rules:**
  * Under G.S. § 105-154(d), a partnership doing business in NC must pay tax on behalf of each nonresident partner on the partner's distributive share of net income at the statutory rate (4.25% for 2025; 3.99% for 2026).
  * **Form NC-NPA Exemption:** If a nonresident partner is an entity (e.g., corporation, partnership, non-grantor trust, or estate) and timely submits Form NC-NPA (*Nonresident Partner Affirmation*) affirming that it will timely file and pay its own NC return, the partnership is not required to pay tax on that partner's behalf.
* **Pass-Through Estimated Tax Requirements:**
  * **Standard (Non-Electing) Entities:** A partnership is not required to make estimated income tax payments; estimated tax payments are also not required on behalf of nonresident shareholders participating in an S Corporation composite return.
  * **Taxed Pass-Through Entities (PTET):** An electing Taxed Partnership or Taxed S Corporation that reasonably expects to have an NC income tax liability of **$500 or more** must pay estimated tax.
  * **Installment Due Dates (Calendar-Year Filers):** Four equal installments due on or before the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months (April 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15).
  * **Payment Forms:** 
    * Form NC-40 PTE for Taxed Partnerships.
    * Form CD-429 PTE for Taxed S Corporations.
    * Form NC-429B PTE to compute any underpayment interest.
* **Individual Estimated Tax Rule (for reference):** Individuals must pay estimated tax via Form NC-40 if expected tax due (net of withholding and credits) is **$1,000 or more**; calendar-year installments are due April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15 of the following year.
* **Applicability:** Applies to Tax Years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * [NCDOR: Form NC-40 PTE Instructions](https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/partnership-tax/partnership-tax-forms-and-instructions/nc-40-pte-taxed-partnership-estimated-income-tax)

### 6. Main Tax Return Forms
* **Individual:**
